thm:smooth-gradient-relaxation-dirichlet.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-10. The normal contraction is mollified on the real line (Energy.NormalContraction.smoothed, via LipschitzApproximation.mollify with the Lebesgue measure): it is smooth, 1-Lipschitz and uniformly within 2/(j+1) of the contraction. Composing a smooth test with it gives a smooth test (SmoothGradient.Test.compSmoothed) whose gradient norm is pointwise not larger, hence with energy at most that of the test, and whose L^2 class converges to the contracted class. This is the relaxed contraction bound on realized tests (SmoothGradient.relaxedContractionBound), and the certified contraction-transfer theorem gives Energy.Markovian and Energy.Dirichlet for Energy.SmoothGradient.relaxation mu for every Borel probability law, including singular laws and dimension zero; the intrinsic-affine relaxation SmoothGradient.Intrinsic.energy mu inherits the property because intrinsic coordinates commute with contractions. No Cheeger identification, Poincare inequality or Markov property of the covariance-weighted relaxations is claimed.

lem:affine-poincare-translation-invarian.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-08. (tau_b)_# mu is Probability.translateLaw mu b. The translated law is log-concave by transporting compact-set log-concavity along the inverse translation (KLS.LogConcave.translateLaw); its affine support is the translated affine support with the same direction (Probability.affineSupport_translateLaw, Probability.direction_affineSupport_translateLaw); its intrinsic law is the translate, inside the direction space, of the image of the intrinsic law of mu under the linear isometric identification of the two direction submodules (Probability.intrinsicMeasure_translateLaw). The certificate packages all of these; no Poincare inequality, isotropic reduction or KLS statement is claimed.

thm:affine-isotropic-reduction.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-08. The three items are KLS.IsotropicBound K, KLS.CovarianceBound K and KLS.AffineBound K, each quantified over every finite-dimensional Euclidean space of one fixed universe. (1) => (3): the intrinsic law is centered inside its direction space (translation transport of the covariance relaxation, certified with thm:affine-covariance-relaxation-closed) and whitened by the self-adjoint whitening equivalence of the positive definite intrinsic covariance (Covariance.exists_whitening, spectral theorem; positivity from lem:ambient-intrinsic-covariance); the covariance relaxation and its optimal constant are transported along continuous linear equivalences (Probability.mapContinuousLinearEquiv, Energy.CovarianceGradient.relaxation_mapContinuousLinearEquiv); the whitened law is isotropic and log-concave and its covariance relaxation is the identity-weighted Lipschitz gradient relaxation, whose optimal constant is the legacy smooth-test constant and hence the literature constant (Poincare.SmoothTest.constant_eq_lipschitzGradient_constant via the certified smooth approximation lemma, then LogConcave.smoothTest_constant_eq_localSlope). (3) => (2): the literature constant of mu is the optimal constant of the Lipschitz gradient relaxation of the intrinsic law, the covariance relaxation is at most ||Sigma|| times it (PreEnergy.sequentialRelaxation_comp_le_mul), and ||Sigma|| = ||Cov_mu||. (2) => (1): an isotropic law has covariance operator 1 of norm at most one. The certificate also shows that AffineBound K in universe zero implies KLS.Conjecture. Dimension zero is included. lem:affine-poincare-translation-invariance is a declared dependency but is not invoked by the Lean proof, which centers the intrinsic law directly; the truth of any item for some K is not claimed.

lem:conditional-fiber-form.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-11. KLS/ConditionalFiber/Closed.lean packages the form of def:conditional-fiber-form as the extended functional KLS.ConditionalFiber.functional mu rho on L^2(mu) and proves Energy.Dirichlet mu (functional mu rho): dense finite domain, lower semicontinuity, the extended quadratic identities and the normal-contraction (Markov) property, for every Borel probability law mu on a finite-dimensional inner-product space and every probability law rho on the unit sphere (no log-concavity, density, second moment or frame identity is used; the Blueprint scope is a typed application in the certificate). The route is the jump representation energyAt_eq_jump_div: on a nondegenerate fiber the normalized variance is the squared jump integral against the two-point measure (kappa b) x (kappa b) divided by 2 Var(id), by the new two-point variance identity Probability.two_mul_evariance_eq_lintegral_prod (Probability/TwoPointVariance.lean, valid in [0, infinity] without square integrability). Symmetry and reversibility are read as this representation and the swap invariance twoPointMeasure_swap. Closedness pushes an almost-everywhere convergent subsequence (TendstoInMeasure.exists_seq_tendsto_ae) through the joint law and the disintegration (Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_compProd) and applies Fatou (lintegral_liminf_le) on the two-point space and on the base law; Lipschitz tests have energy at most d L^2 (energy_le_of_lipschitzWith), so the smooth compactly supported core (WeightedGradient.dense_smoothCore) lies in the finite domain. No comparison with a gradient energy, no fiber Poincare input, no frame bound and no Poincare inequality is claimed.

lem:conditional-fiber-energy-comparison.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-11. KLS/ConditionalFiber/EnergyComparison.lean states the fiber hypothesis as FiberBound mu rho kappa (for baseLaw-almost every nondegenerate fiber, Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant of the fiber law <= kappa * evariance id) and proves energy_le_of_fiberBound (energy mu rho f <= kappa * Energy.LocalSlope.energy mu f, finite, for every Energy.LocalSlope.Admissible test) and literatureConstant_le_of_fiberBound (a form-gap bound C on domain mu rho gives Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant mu <= kappa * C), for mu absolutely continuous with respect to a Haar measure and an admissible frame rho. The route: Poincare.LocalSlope.Holds transports across a measure-preserving isometric equivalence (MeasurePreserving.lintegral_comp_emb, Function.Surjective.iSup_comp on the local-slope definition), so for a law with full affine support the intrinsic constant is the infimum of its coordinate constants and ENNReal.iInf_mul turns a finite bound on that infimum into the per-test inequality; full support follows from Measure.addHaar_affineSubspace for mu and from nonzero variance for the real fibers (Submodule.finrank_lt on a proper direction of R). The line slice t -> f(z + t theta) has local slope |<theta, grad f>| at Rademacher points (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt, HasDerivAt.hasGradientAt, the existing apply_eq_norm_gradient); the Rademacher null set and square integrability pass through the joint law and Measure.ae_ae_of_ae_compProd; Measure.lintegral_compProd, lintegral_map with reconstruct_coordinates, lintegral_prod_symm and the frame identity (ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal) give kappa times the gradient energy, identified with the local-slope energy by energy_eq_lintegral_gradient. The second conclusion is proved directly on Poincare.LocalSlope.Holds through form_toLp, L2.variance_toLp and ofReal_variance. No value of kappa, no log-concavity, no fiber Poincare input and no KLS statement is claimed.

cor:conditional-fiber-twelve-bound.note: Proved in Lean on 2026-09-11 and registered on 2026-09-12. KLS/LogConcave/ConditionalFiber.lean proves ae_conditionalFiber_logConcave (for baseLaw-almost every base point the chosen conditional kernel kernel mu rho b is a compact-set log-concave law on R) and derives conditionalFiber_fiberBound_four (FiberBound mu rho 4), conditionalFiber_energy_le_four_mul, conditionalFiber_literatureConstant_le_four_mul and the literal 12 versions with the _of_four suffix. Three pieces of new infrastructure close the gaps recorded on 2026-09-11. (1) Probability/Line/BrunnMinkowski.lean proves compact one-dimensional Brunn-Minkowski (translate K by inf L and L by sup K inside K + L; the two translates meet in a single point, so measure_union_add_inter with translation invariance gives vol K + vol L <= vol (K + L)), its inner-regular convex-combination form, and the fully general one-dimensional Prekopa-Leindler inequality (layer cake lintegral_eq_lintegral_meas_lt, the level-set inclusion t {f > s} + (1-t) {g > s} subset {h > s}, normalization of both factors to supremum one by homogeneity, truncation with monotone convergence for unbounded factors, and a two-term ENNReal AM-GM proved from NNReal.geom_mean_le_arith_mean2_weighted). KLS/LogConcave/Line/OfDensity.lean applies it to indicator multiples of a Borell density and gives LineDensity.logConcave, the converse of the existing LogConcave.exists_lineDensity. (2) Probability/HaarLine.lean builds the linear equivalence (R theta)-perp x R = E, (z, s) -> z + s theta, and proves exists_lintegral_line: for a unit theta there is a positive finite c with c * integral G dm = double integral of G(z + s theta) against addHaar and volume (ContinuousLinearEquiv.isAddHaarMeasure_map, Measure.isAddLeftInvariant_eq_smul, addHaarScalarFactor_pos_of_isAddHaarMeasure); c depends on theta and is never evaluated, and the proof never needs measurability of theta -> c. (3) KLS/ConditionalFiber/SliceKernel.lean defines sliceMass, SliceGood, sliceDensity and the Markov kernel sliceKernel (Kernel.withDensity of the normalized line density on the good set, Kernel.piecewise with a Dirac law elsewhere) and proves compProd_baseLaw_sliceKernel (baseLaw ⊗ₘ sliceKernel = jointLaw) by reducing both sides, for each fixed direction, to the same iterated integral through exists_lintegral_line; finiteness of the slice mass almost everywhere is the case G = 1 of that identity. ae_sliceKernel_eq is then ProbabilityTheory.eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd. Assembly: absolute continuity gives full affine support (affineSupport_eq_top_of_absolutelyContinuous, made public in EnergyComparison.lean without a type change) and hence a Borell density; on a good base point the normalized line density is a Borell density of the slice kernel (upper semicontinuity by UpperSemicontinuous.comp and Continuous.comp_upperSemicontinuous, log-concavity along the affine reconstruction map), so LineDensity.logConcave applies; the remaining base points carry a Dirac law and KLS.logConcave_dirac covers them, so no exceptional set is discarded. The Blueprint corollary is restated with the sharp constant 4; 12 is the immediate weakening. No frame bound, no Poincare inequality for mu and no KLS statement is claimed; q:conditional-fiber-frame remains open.
